ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The attached table has two columns, labeled Ion and Ionic Radius (pm). It lists Cl− with radius 181 pm, I− with radius 216 pm, S2− with radius 184 pm, and Te2− with radius 221 pm. Reasoning: By Coulomb's law, stronger ion-water attraction is favored by larger charge magnitude and shorter distance between charges. The 2− anions should interact more strongly with polar water molecules than the 1− anions, all else equal. Comparing the two 2− anions, S2− has a smaller ionic radius than Te2−, 184 pm versus 221 pm, so water molecules can approach its charge more closely. Therefore S2− is most likely to have the strongest interactions with nearby water molecules.

Therefore select S2− as having the strongest interactions with nearby water molecules.
